solution:
The relation \(x^3 + y^3 = 4ax\) has one arbitrary constant \(a\), so differentiate once and eliminate \(a\).

From the given equation, \(4a = \dfrac{x^3 + y^3}{x}\).

Differentiate \(x^3 + y^3 = 4ax\) with respect to \(x\):
\(3x^2 + 3y^2\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4a\).

Substitute \(4a = \dfrac{x^3 + y^3}{x}\):
\(3x^2 + 3y^2\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x^3 + y^3}{x}\).

Multiply both sides by \(x\):
\(3x^3 + 3xy^2\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x^3 + y^3\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(3xy^2\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y^3 - 2x^3\), i.e. \(3xy^2\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2x^3 - y^3 = 0\).

The relation \(Ax^2 + By^2 = 1\) has two arbitrary constants \(A\) and \(B\), so differentiate twice.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(2Ax + 2By\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\), i.e. \(Ax + By\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\). \(\quad(1)\)

Differentiate \((1)\) with respect to \(x\):
\(A + B\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + By\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\). \(\quad(2)\)

From \((1)\): \(A = -\dfrac{By}{x}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\). Substitute in \((2)\):
\(-\dfrac{By}{x}\dfrac{dy}{dx} + B\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + By\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\).

Divide by \(B\) and multiply by \(x\):
\(-y\dfrac{dy}{dx} + x\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + xy\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(xy\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + x\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 - y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

The relation \(y = A\cos(\log x) + B\sin(\log x)\) has two arbitrary constants, so differentiate twice.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -A\sin(\log x)\cdot\dfrac{1}{x} + B\cos(\log x)\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\).

\(\therefore x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -A\sin(\log x) + B\cos(\log x)\). \(\quad(1)\)

Differentiate \((1)\) with respect to \(x\):
\(x\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -A\cos(\log x)\cdot\dfrac{1}{x} - B\sin(\log x)\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\).

The right side is \(-\dfrac{1}{x}\big(A\cos(\log x) + B\sin(\log x)\big) = -\dfrac{y}{x}\).

\(\therefore x\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{y}{x}\).

Multiply by \(x\):
\(x^2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is \(x^2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0\).

The relation \(y^2 = (x + c)^3\) has one arbitrary constant \(c\), so differentiate once and eliminate \(c\).

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3(x + c)^2\). \(\quad(1)\)

From the given equation, \((x + c)^3 = y^2\), so \((x + c) = y^{2/3}\) and \((x + c)^2 = y^{4/3}\).

A cleaner elimination: from \((1)\), \((x + c)^2 = \dfrac{2y}{3}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\), so \((x + c)^3 = (x+c)\cdot\dfrac{2y}{3}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\). Instead cube \((1)\) and square the original to eliminate \((x+c)\):

Cube \((1)\): \(\left(2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3 = 27(x + c)^6 = 27\big[(x + c)^3\big]^2 = 27(y^2)^2 = 27y^4\).

\(\therefore 8y^3\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3 = 27y^4\).

Divide by \(y^3\):
\(8\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3 = 27y\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is \(8\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3 = 27y\).

The relation \(c_1 x^3 + c_2 y^2 = 5\) has two arbitrary constants \(c_1\) and \(c_2\), so differentiate twice.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(3c_1 x^2 + 2c_2 y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\). \(\quad(1)\)

Differentiate \((1)\) with respect to \(x\):
\(6c_1 x + 2c_2\left[\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + y\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right] = 0\). \(\quad(2)\)

From \((1)\): \(c_1 x^2 = -\dfrac{2c_2 y}{3}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\), so \(c_1 x = -\dfrac{2c_2 y}{3x}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\). Substitute in \((2)\):
\(6\left(-\dfrac{2c_2 y}{3x}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) + 2c_2\left[\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + y\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right] = 0\).

\(-\dfrac{4c_2 y}{x}\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2c_2\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + 2c_2 y\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\).

Divide by \(2c_2\) and multiply by \(x\):
\(-2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} + x\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + xy\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(xy\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + x\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 - 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

The relation \(y = Ae^{5x} + Be^{-5x}\) has two arbitrary constants, so differentiate twice.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 5Ae^{5x} - 5Be^{-5x}\).

Differentiate again:
\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 25Ae^{5x} + 25Be^{-5x} = 25\big(Ae^{5x} + Be^{-5x}\big) = 25y\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is \(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 25y = 0\).

The relation \((y - a)^2 = 4(x - b)\) has two arbitrary constants \(a\) and \(b\), so differentiate twice.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(2(y - a)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4\), i.e. \((y - a)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2\). \(\quad(1)\)

Differentiate \((1)\) with respect to \(x\):
\((y - a)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \dfrac{dy}{dx}\cdot\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

\(\therefore (y - a)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = 0\). \(\quad(2)\)

From \((1)\), \((y - a) = \dfrac{2}{\,dy/dx\,}\). Substitute in \((2)\):
\(\dfrac{2}{\,dy/dx\,}\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = 0\).

Multiply by \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\):
\(2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3 = 0\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is \(2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3 = 0\).

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed answer key gives \((x^2+xy)\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=0\); the correct differential equation is \((x^2+x)\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=0\) (derived below).]

The relation \(y = a + \dfrac{a}{x}\) has one arbitrary constant \(a\), so differentiate once and eliminate \(a\).

Write \(y = a\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right) = a\cdot\dfrac{x + 1}{x}\).

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = a\left(-\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right) = -\dfrac{a}{x^2}\).

So \(a = -x^2\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

Substitute in \(y = a\cdot\dfrac{x + 1}{x}\):
\(y = -x^2\dfrac{dy}{dx}\cdot\dfrac{x + 1}{x} = -x(x + 1)\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(x(x + 1)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0\).

The relation \(y = c_1 e^{2x} + c_2 e^{5x}\) has two arbitrary constants, so differentiate twice.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2c_1 e^{2x} + 5c_2 e^{5x}\). \(\quad(1)\)

Differentiate again:
\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 4c_1 e^{2x} + 25c_2 e^{5x}\). \(\quad(2)\)

Eliminate \(c_1 e^{2x}\) and \(c_2 e^{5x}\). The roots \(2\) and \(5\) satisfy \(m^2 - 7m + 10 = 0\), so the operator gives:
\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 7\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 10y\)
\(= \big(4c_1 e^{2x} + 25c_2 e^{5x}\big) - 7\big(2c_1 e^{2x} + 5c_2 e^{5x}\big) + 10\big(c_1 e^{2x} + c_2 e^{5x}\big)\)
\(= c_1 e^{2x}(4 - 14 + 10) + c_2 e^{5x}(25 - 35 + 10) = 0\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 7\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 10y = 0\).

The relation \(y = e^{-2x}(A\cos x + B\sin x)\) has two arbitrary constants, so differentiate twice.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -2e^{-2x}(A\cos x + B\sin x) + e^{-2x}(-A\sin x + B\cos x)\).

The first term is \(-2y\), so
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -2y + e^{-2x}(-A\sin x + B\cos x)\).

\(\therefore e^{-2x}(-A\sin x + B\cos x) = \dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2y\). \(\quad(1)\)

Differentiate again:
\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -2\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[e^{-2x}(-A\sin x + B\cos x)\Big]\).

Now \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\Big[e^{-2x}(-A\sin x + B\cos x)\Big] = -2e^{-2x}(-A\sin x + B\cos x) + e^{-2x}(-A\cos x - B\sin x)\).

Using \((1)\) for the first part and \(e^{-2x}(A\cos x + B\sin x) = y\) for the second:
\(= -2\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2y\right) - y\).

Hence
\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -2\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2y\right) - y = -4\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 5y\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 4\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 5y = 0\).

A line making an intercept \(a\) on the X-axis passes through \((a, 0)\). Its equation, with slope as a parameter, can be written using the X-intercept form. Taking the family in intercept form on the X-axis:
\(\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 1\) with fixed \(a\) and variable \(b\), i.e. \(bx + ay = ab\) with \(a\) constant.

Write the line as \(y = m(x - a)\), where \(m\) is the arbitrary constant (the family passes through the fixed point \((a, 0)\)).

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = m\).

Substitute \(m = \dfrac{dy}{dx}\) into \(y = m(x - a)\):
\(y = (x - a)\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\((x - a)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y\).

A parabola with axis parallel to the X-axis and latus rectum \(4a\) has the form
\((y - k)^2 = 4a(x - h)\),
where \(h\) and \(k\) are arbitrary constants (\(a\) is fixed). Two constants, so differentiate twice.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(2(y - k)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4a\), i.e. \((y - k)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2a\). \(\quad(1)\)

Differentiate \((1)\) with respect to \(x\):
\((y - k)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = 0\). \(\quad(2)\)

From \((1)\), \((y - k) = \dfrac{2a}{\,dy/dx\,}\). Substitute in \((2)\):
\(\dfrac{2a}{\,dy/dx\,}\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = 0\).

Multiply by \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\):
\(2a\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3 = 0\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(2a\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3 = 0\).

For the ellipse, the major axis is twice the minor axis, so the semi-major axis \(= 2\times\) semi-minor axis. Take the ellipse centred at the origin with axes along the coordinate axes:
\(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\), with \(a = 2b\) (major along X-axis).

Then \(\dfrac{x^2}{4b^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\), i.e. \(x^2 + 4y^2 = 4b^2\). One arbitrary constant \(b\), so differentiate once.

Differentiate \(x^2 + 4y^2 = 4b^2\) with respect to \(x\):
\(2x + 8y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

Divide by \(2\):
\(x + 4y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(x + 4y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

All lines parallel to \(2x + 3y + 4 = 0\) have the same slope. The slope of the given line is \(-\dfrac{2}{3}\).

The family is \(2x + 3y + c = 0\), where \(c\) is the arbitrary constant.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(2 + 3\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(3\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2 = 0\), i.e. \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{2}{3}\).

A circle of radius \(9\) with centre \(A(h, k)\) has equation
\((x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = 81\),
where \(h\) and \(k\) are arbitrary constants. Two constants, so differentiate twice.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(2(x - h) + 2(y - k)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\), i.e. \((x - h) + (y - k)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\). \(\quad(1)\)

Differentiate \((1)\) with respect to \(x\):
\(1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + (y - k)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 0\).

\(\therefore (y - k) = -\dfrac{1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2}{\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}}\). \(\quad(2)\)

From \((1)\), \((x - h) = -(y - k)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]\dfrac{dy}{dx}}{\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}}\). \(\quad(3)\)

Substitute \((2)\) and \((3)\) into \((x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = 81\):
\(\dfrac{\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^2\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2}{\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^2} + \dfrac{\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^2}{\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^2} = 81\).

The left side factors as \(\dfrac{\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^2\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]}{\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^2} = \dfrac{\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^3}{\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^2}\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(\left[1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^3 = 81\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^2\).

The family of all parabolas whose axis is the X-axis is \(y^2 = 4a(x - h)\), where \(a\) and \(h\) are arbitrary constants (\((h, 0)\) is the vertex, \(4a\) the latus rectum). Since there are two arbitrary constants, differentiate twice.

Differentiate: \(2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 4a\).

Differentiate again: \(2\left[\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + y\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right] = 0\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is \(y\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = 0\).

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed answer key gives \(xy\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+x\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2-2y\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0\); the correct coefficient of the last term is \(-1\), giving \(xy\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+x\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2-y\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0\) (below).]

The relation \(y^2 = a(b - x)(b + x) = a(b^2 - x^2)\) has two arbitrary constants (\(a\) and the product \(ab^2\)), so differentiate twice.

Write \(y^2 = ab^2 - ax^2\).

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -2ax\), i.e. \(y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -ax\). \(\quad(1)\)

Differentiate \((1)\) with respect to \(x\):
\(y\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = -a\). \(\quad(2)\)

From \((1)\), \(a = -\dfrac{y}{x}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\). Substitute in \((2)\):
\(y\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = \dfrac{y}{x}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

Multiply by \(x\):
\(xy\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + x\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 - y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(xy\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + x\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 - y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

The relation \(y = a\sin(x + b)\) has two arbitrary constants \(a\) and \(b\), so differentiate twice.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = a\cos(x + b)\).

Differentiate again:
\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -a\sin(x + b) = -y\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + y = 0\).

[Textbook answer-key note: the printed answer \((y-a)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2=0\) still contains the arbitrary constant \(a\); the fully-reduced equation is \(2(x+4)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0\) (below).]

The relation \((y - a)^2 = b(x + 4)\) has two arbitrary constants \(a\) and \(b\), so differentiate twice and eliminate both.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(2(y - a)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = b\). \(\quad(1)\)

Differentiate \((1)\) with respect to \(x\) (\(b\) is constant):
\((y - a)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 = 0\). \(\quad(2)\)

From \((2)\): \((y - a) = -\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2}{\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}}\).

From \((1)\): \(b = 2(y - a)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{2\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3}{\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}}\).

Substitute \((y - a)^2 = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^4}{\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^2}\) and the value of \(b\) into the original equation \((y - a)^2 = b(x + 4)\):
\(\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^4}{\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^2} = -\dfrac{2\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3}{\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}}(x + 4)\).

Divide both sides by \(\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3}{\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}}\):
\(\dfrac{\dfrac{dy}{dx}}{\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}} = -2(x + 4)\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -2(x + 4)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\), i.e. \(2(x + 4)\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed answer key gives \(2x^2y\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+2x^2\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2+y=0\), which does not match this stem; the correct equation is \(x^2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=0\) (below).]

The relation \(y = \sqrt{a}\cos(\log x) + b\sin(\log x)\) has two arbitrary constants (\(\sqrt{a}\) and \(b\)), so differentiate twice. Let \(A = \sqrt{a}\) and \(B = b\), so \(y = A\cos(\log x) + B\sin(\log x)\).

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -A\sin(\log x)\cdot\dfrac{1}{x} + B\cos(\log x)\cdot\dfrac{1}{x}\).

\(\therefore x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -A\sin(\log x) + B\cos(\log x)\). \(\quad(1)\)

Differentiate \((1)\) with respect to \(x\):
\(x\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{1}{x}\big(A\cos(\log x) + B\sin(\log x)\big) = -\dfrac{y}{x}\).

Multiply by \(x\):
\(x^2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(x^2\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 0\).

The relation \(y = Ae^{3x + 1} + Be^{-3x + 1}\) has two arbitrary constants. Write \(y = e\big(Ae^{3x} + Be^{-3x}\big)\); absorbing \(e\) into constants, \(y = A_1 e^{3x} + B_1 e^{-3x}\), so differentiate twice.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3Ae^{3x + 1} - 3Be^{-3x + 1}\).

Differentiate again:
\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 9Ae^{3x + 1} + 9Be^{-3x + 1} = 9\big(Ae^{3x + 1} + Be^{-3x + 1}\big) = 9y\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 9y = 0\).

A circle passing through the origin with centre on the X-axis has centre \((a, 0)\) and radius \(a\) (so that it passes through the origin). Its equation is
\((x - a)^2 + y^2 = a^2\), i.e. \(x^2 - 2ax + y^2 = 0\), i.e. \(x^2 + y^2 = 2ax\).

One arbitrary constant \(a\), so differentiate once. From the equation, \(2a = \dfrac{x^2 + y^2}{x}\).

Differentiate \(x^2 + y^2 = 2ax\) with respect to \(x\):
\(2x + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2a = \dfrac{x^2 + y^2}{x}\).

Multiply by \(x\):
\(2x^2 + 2xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x^2 + y^2\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(x^2 + 2xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} = y^2\), i.e. \(2xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} + x^2 - y^2 = 0\).

A parabola with latus rectum \(4b\) and axis parallel to the Y-axis has the form
\((x - h)^2 = 4b(y - k)\),
where \(h\) and \(k\) are arbitrary constants (\(b\) is fixed). Two constants, so differentiate twice.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(2(x - h) = 4b\dfrac{dy}{dx}\), i.e. \((x - h) = 2b\dfrac{dy}{dx}\). \(\quad(1)\)

Differentiate \((1)\) with respect to \(x\):
\(1 = 2b\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(2b\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 1\).

For the ellipse, the major axis is twice the minor axis, so the semi-major axis \(= 2\times\) semi-minor axis. Take the ellipse centred at the origin with axes along the coordinate axes:
\(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) with \(a = 2b\) (major along X-axis).

Then \(\dfrac{x^2}{4b^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\), i.e. \(x^2 + 4y^2 = 4b^2\). One arbitrary constant \(b\), so differentiate once.

Differentiate \(x^2 + 4y^2 = 4b^2\) with respect to \(x\):
\(2x + 8y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

Divide by \(2\):
\(x + 4y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(x + 4y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

All lines parallel to \(3x - 2y + 7 = 0\) have the same slope. The slope of the given line is \(\dfrac{3}{2}\).

The family is \(3x - 2y + c = 0\), where \(c\) is the arbitrary constant.

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):
\(3 - 2\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(2\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 3 = 0\), i.e. \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{3}{2}\).

The given hyperbola is \(\dfrac{x^2}{16} - \dfrac{y^2}{36} = k\), i.e. \(\dfrac{x^2}{16k} - \dfrac{y^2}{36k} = 1\). Its transverse axis length is \(2\sqrt{16k} = 8\sqrt{k}\) and conjugate axis length is \(2\sqrt{36k} = 12\sqrt{k}\).

The required hyperbola has transverse and conjugate axes half of these, so its \(a^2\) and \(b^2\) become one-quarter of the originals: \(a^2 = \dfrac{16k}{4} = 4k\) and \(b^2 = \dfrac{36k}{4} = 9k\). Thus the family is
\(\dfrac{x^2}{4k} - \dfrac{y^2}{9k} = 1\), i.e. \(9x^2 - 4y^2 = 36k\), with \(k\) arbitrary.

One arbitrary constant \(k\), so differentiate once.

Differentiate \(9x^2 - 4y^2 = 36k\) with respect to \(x\):
\(18x - 8y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

Divide by \(2\):
\(9x - 4y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\).

\(\therefore\) the required differential equation is
\(9x - 4y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\), i.e. \(4y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 9x\).
